questions.prompt: Which word names a person?
questions.explanation: A noun can name a person. Teacher names a person who helps learners.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify nouns that name people in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence starts with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: A sentence should begin with a capital letter.
questions.learningOutcome: Use capital letters at the beginning of sentences.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct greeting for morning.
questions.explanation: Good morning is used when greeting someone early in the day.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common greetings appropriately in daily conversations.

questions.prompt: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
questions.explanation: A question mark shows that a sentence asks something.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize punctuation marks used in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word means the opposite of happy?
questions.explanation: Sad is an antonym of happy because it gives the opposite meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple antonyms in familiar contexts.

questions.prompt: Which word is a verb?
questions.explanation: A verb shows an action. Jump is something a person can do.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify action verbs in simple word groups.

questions.prompt: Which word is a colour?
questions.explanation: Yellow names a colour, like the colour of a ripe banana.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common describing words for colour.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: School is the correct spelling of the place where learners study.
questions.learningOutcome: Spell familiar school vocabulary correctly.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with cat?
questions.explanation: Cat and hat have the same ending sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple rhyming words by listening to ending sounds.

questions.prompt: Which word shows one item?
questions.explanation: Book is singular because it means one item.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish singular nouns from plural nouns.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? I brush my teeth with a ____.
questions.explanation: A toothbrush is the tool used to clean teeth.
questions.learningOutcome: Use context to choose familiar everyday vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which polite word should you use when asking for help?
questions.explanation: Please makes a request polite.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite words when making simple requests.

questions.prompt: Which word names a place?
questions.explanation: A noun can name a place. Market names a place where people buy and sell things.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify nouns that name places in familiar contexts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a command?
questions.explanation: A command tells someone to do something.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize simple command sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is a pronoun?
questions.explanation: She is a pronoun because it can stand for the name of a girl or woman.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common personal pronouns in sentences.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: The pupils ____ in the classroom.
questions.explanation: Pupils means more than one learner, so the correct verb is are.
questions.learningOutcome: Use is, am, and are correctly with simple subjects.

questions.prompt: Choose the plural of mango.
questions.explanation: Many nouns ending in o take es to form the plural.
questions.learningOutcome: Form plurals of common nouns by adding s or es.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a full stop correctly?
questions.explanation: A statement ends with a full stop.
questions.learningOutcome: Punctuate simple statements correctly.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? Amina sat ____ the chair.
questions.explanation: On shows the position of Amina in relation to the chair.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common prepositions of place in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of clean?
questions.explanation: Dirty has the opposite meaning of clean.
questions.learningOutcome: Use antonyms to build meaning in simple texts.

questions.prompt: Choose the past tense of play.
questions.explanation: Played shows that the action happened before now.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple past tense forms of regular verbs.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses I correctly?
questions.explanation: The pronoun I is always written as a capital letter and agrees with am.
questions.learningOutcome: Write the pronoun I correctly in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word best describes a tall tree?
questions.explanation: Tall is an adjective because it describes the tree.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify adjectives that describe nouns.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word: The baby is ____.
questions.explanation: Is crying shows an action happening now.
questions.learningOutcome: Use present continuous tense in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which pair has words with the same meaning?
questions.explanation: Small and little are synonyms because they have nearly the same meaning.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize simple synonyms in familiar word pairs.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? We went to school ____ Monday.
questions.explanation: On is used with days of the week.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common prepositions of time in everyday sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written in the present tense?
questions.explanation: Reads shows an action that happens now or often.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple present tense in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Choose the word with the /ch/ sound.
questions.explanation: Chair begins with the /ch/ sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common consonant sounds in words.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
questions.explanation: A clear sentence usually places the doer before the action and object.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange words to make meaningful simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is a compound word?
questions.explanation: Football is made from two words: foot and ball.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple compound words in familiar vocabulary.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? My sister ____ breakfast every morning.
questions.explanation: Sister is one person, so the simple present verb takes s.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple present verbs correctly with singular subjects.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a comma correctly in a list?
options: I bought maize, beans and rice.
I bought, maize beans and rice.
I bought maize beans, and rice
I, bought maize beans and rice.
questions.correctAnswer: I bought maize, beans and rice.
questions.explanation: A comma can separate items in a list.
questions.learningOutcome: Use commas to separate items in simple lists.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that means to speak softly.
questions.explanation: To whisper means to speak in a very soft voice.
questions.learningOutcome: Use words that describe ways of speaking.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The cat ran ____ the table.
questions.explanation: Under shows where the cat ran.
questions.learningOutcome: Use prepositions of place to show location.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a question?
questions.explanation: A question asks for information and usually ends with a question mark.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify questions in everyday communication.

questions.prompt: Which word is the correct plural of box?
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in x usually add es to form the plural.
questions.learningOutcome: Form plurals of nouns ending in x.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? That bag is ____ than mine.
questions.explanation: Heavier compares two things, the two bags.
questions.learningOutcome: Use comparative adjectives to compare two objects.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with the correct capital letter for a name.
questions.explanation: Names of people and places begin with capital letters.
questions.learningOutcome: Use capital letters for proper nouns.

questions.prompt: Which word can replace children in this sentence? The children are playing.
questions.explanation: They is used for more than one person.
questions.learningOutcome: Use pronouns to replace plural nouns.

questions.prompt: Which phrase shows polite disagreement?
options: I think there is another way.
questions.correctAnswer: I think there is another way.
questions.explanation: Polite disagreement shares a different idea without insulting anyone.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful language during classroom discussions.

questions.prompt: Read the sentence: The tired farmer rested under a tree. Which word describes the farmer?
questions.explanation: Tired describes the farmer, so it is an adjective.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify descriptive words in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence joins the ideas correctly?
options: It rained, so we stayed indoors.
It rained so we stayed indoors?
It rained we stayed indoors so.
So it rained we stayed indoors.
questions.correctAnswer: It rained, so we stayed indoors.
questions.explanation: So can join a cause to its result in a clear sentence.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple conjunctions to join related ideas.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The girls ____ their books yesterday.
questions.explanation: Yesterday shows past time, so the verb should be carried.
questions.learningOutcome: Use past tense verbs with time words such as yesterday.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
questions.explanation: An apostrophe and s can show that one person owns something.
questions.learningOutcome: Use apostrophes to show simple possession.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The class was quiet ____ the teacher spoke.
questions.explanation: While shows that two things happened at the same time.
questions.learningOutcome: Use conjunctions to connect ideas in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the adjective in the correct place?
questions.explanation: In English, many adjectives come before the noun they describe.
questions.learningOutcome: Place adjectives correctly before nouns in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: Njeri watered the sukuma wiki before school. What did Njeri do?
questions.explanation: The sentence says Njeri watered the sukuma wiki.
questions.learningOutcome: Answer direct questions from a short sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same beginning sound as shop?
questions.explanation: Shop and ship both begin with the /sh/ sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify shared beginning sounds in common words.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct order to make a sentence: planted / trees / We
questions.explanation: The sentence begins with the doer, then the action, then the object.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange jumbled words into meaningful sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? I have ____ orange and a banana.
questions.explanation: An is used before a word that begins with a vowel sound, such as orange.
questions.learningOutcome: Use a and an correctly before common nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the correct form of go?
options: They go to church on Sunday.
They goes to church on Sunday.
They going to church on Sunday.
They gone to church on Sunday.
questions.correctAnswer: They go to church on Sunday.
questions.explanation: They is plural, so the simple present verb is go.
questions.learningOutcome: Use base verbs correctly with plural subjects.

questions.prompt: Which word is formed by adding the prefix un- to kind?
questions.explanation: The prefix un- can change a word to mean not, so unkind means not kind.
questions.learningOutcome: Use common prefixes to understand word meanings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is best for thanking a friend?
questions.explanation: This sentence expresses thanks clearly and politely.
questions.learningOutcome: Use polite expressions for appreciation.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a mistake in capitalization?
questions.explanation: The first word of a sentence should start with a capital letter.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify capitalization errors in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The children shared the mangoes ____.
questions.explanation: Fairly is an adverb that tells how the children shared.
questions.learningOutcome: Use adverbs to describe how actions are done.

questions.prompt: Read: The sky became dark and the wind blew. What might happen next?
options: The road may turn into sugar.
questions.explanation: Dark sky and wind are common signs that rain may come.
questions.learningOutcome: Make simple predictions using clues from a sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word is the odd one out?
questions.explanation: Chair is furniture, while the other words are fruits.
questions.learningOutcome: Group words by meaning and identify the odd one out.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
questions.explanation: Quotation marks show the exact words spoken.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize quotation marks in simple direct speech.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? This is the ____ building in our school.
questions.explanation: Tallest compares one building with all the others.
questions.learningOutcome: Use superlative adjectives to compare more than two items.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows future time?
options: We will visit the library tomorrow.
We are visiting the library now.
questions.correctAnswer: We will visit the library tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Will visit and tomorrow show an action that has not happened yet.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple future tense in familiar sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? There is ____ milk in the cup.
questions.explanation: Some can be used with uncountable nouns such as milk.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns.

questions.prompt: Which word has the same meaning as begin?
questions.explanation: Begin and start are synonyms.
questions.learningOutcome: Use synonyms to understand word meanings.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the best opening for a friendly letter?
questions.explanation: A friendly letter often begins with Dear followed by the person's name.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize parts of a simple friendly letter.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The learners listened ____ to the story.
questions.explanation: Carefully tells how the learners listened.
questions.learningOutcome: Use adverbs that describe careful listening and speaking.

questions.prompt: Which option changes the sentence to past tense? I wash my hands.
questions.explanation: Washed shows the action happened in the past.
questions.learningOutcome: Rewrite simple sentences from present to past tense.

questions.prompt: Which word completes the sentence? The old man walked ____ across the road.
questions.explanation: Slowly is an adverb that tells how the old man walked.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose adverbs that describe actions in sentences.

questions.prompt: Read: Otieno missed the bus because he woke up late. Why did Otieno miss the bus?
questions.explanation: The word because gives the reason Otieno missed the bus.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify reasons in short sentences using because.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the word their correctly?
questions.explanation: Their shows that the bags belong to the pupils.
questions.learningOutcome: Use possessive pronouns in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word is a homophone of son?
questions.explanation: Son and sun sound the same but have different meanings.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize common homophones by sound and meaning.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: An exclamation mark can show strong feeling or surprise.
questions.learningOutcome: Use exclamation marks in expressive sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the clearest meaning?
options: After lunch, we cleaned the classroom.
Cleaned after classroom we lunch the.
We after cleaned lunch classroom the.
Lunch cleaned the classroom after we.
questions.correctAnswer: After lunch, we cleaned the classroom.
questions.explanation: The words are arranged in a clear order that shows when and what happened.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose well-ordered sentences that communicate clearly.

questions.prompt: Read: I was as busy as a bee during clean-up. What does the sentence mean?
questions.explanation: As busy as a bee is a simile that means working very hard.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple similes in familiar contexts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines these ideas? I was hungry. I ate a banana.
options: I was hungry, so I ate a banana.
I was hungry but I ate a banana?
I ate hungry because a banana.
A banana was hungry, so I ate.
questions.correctAnswer: I was hungry, so I ate a banana.
questions.explanation: The conjunction so shows the result of being hungry.
questions.learningOutcome: Combine short sentences using suitable conjunctions.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? If it rains, we ____ the match.
questions.explanation: Will stop shows a possible future action after if it rains.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple if sentences to show possible results.

questions.prompt: Which sentence should come first in a paragraph about making tea?
options: After that, pour the tea into a cup.
questions.explanation: The word First signals the beginning step in a process.
questions.learningOutcome: Arrange ideas in a logical order using sequence words.

questions.prompt: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
questions.explanation: Cake, rain, and day have a long a sound, while mat has a short a sound.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare vowel sounds in familiar words.

questions.prompt: Read: The boys packed their balls, boots and water bottles before the game. Which item is not mentioned?
questions.explanation: The sentence mentions balls, boots, and water bottles, but not whistles.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify details that are present or absent in a short text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence changes this command into a polite request? Give me the ruler.
options: Please may I have the ruler?
You must give me the ruler.
questions.correctAnswer: Please may I have the ruler?
questions.explanation: A polite request uses words such as please and may.
questions.learningOutcome: Change direct commands into polite requests.

questions.prompt: Which word best replaces very big in the sentence? The school has a very big hall.
questions.explanation: Huge means very big and makes the sentence stronger.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose precise words to improve meaning.

questions.prompt: Which option corrects this sentence? the goat ate maize in nakuru.
options: The goat ate maize in Nakuru.
The goat ate maize near nakuru.
the goat ate maize in Nakuru today.
The goat ate green maize in nakuru.
questions.correctAnswer: The goat ate maize in Nakuru.
questions.explanation: The first word and the place name Nakuru need capital letters.
questions.learningOutcome: Correct capitalization in sentences with proper nouns.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses both adjectives correctly?
questions.explanation: The adjectives small and brown come before the noun puppy.
questions.learningOutcome: Use two simple adjectives before a noun in a clear order.

questions.prompt: Read: Maria planted seeds, watered them, and waited for them to grow. Which word shows order?
questions.explanation: And connects actions in the order they happened.
questions.learningOutcome: Notice connecting words that link events in a sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses an apostrophe for a contraction?
questions.explanation: Can't is a contraction of cannot and uses an apostrophe.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize contractions in everyday sentences.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? The river was deep, ____ the children did not cross it.
questions.explanation: So links a reason to its result.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose conjunctions that show cause and effect.

questions.prompt: Which topic sentence best fits a paragraph about keeping the classroom clean?
options: We can keep our classroom clean in many ways.
questions.correctAnswer: We can keep our classroom clean in many ways.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence introduces the main idea of the paragraph.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a topic sentence for a simple paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best shows that the speaker is listening actively?
options: I understand that you lost your pencil.
I will talk while you talk.
I am looking away from you.
questions.correctAnswer: I understand that you lost your pencil.
questions.explanation: Active listening shows attention to what the other person has said.
questions.learningOutcome: Show understanding during conversations using suitable responses.

questions.prompt: Which option changes this sentence to future tense? She cooks rice.
questions.explanation: Will cook shows that the action will happen later.
questions.learningOutcome: Rewrite simple present tense sentences in future tense.

questions.prompt: Read: The road was muddy, but the pupils reached school. What does but show?
questions.explanation: But shows a contrast between the muddy road and reaching school.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of simple connectors in sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is the best concluding sentence for a paragraph about washing hands?
options: Clean hands help us stay healthy.
There are clouds in the sky.
questions.correctAnswer: Clean hands help us stay healthy.
questions.explanation: A concluding sentence should close the paragraph by returning to the main idea.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a suitable concluding sentence for a simple paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which word best completes the sentence? Either Asha ____ Kevin will lead the group.
questions.explanation: Either pairs with or to show one choice between two people.
questions.learningOutcome: Use either...or in simple sentences.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best improves this idea? The dog ran.
options: The brown dog ran quickly across the field.
The dog ran and ran and ran and.
questions.correctAnswer: The brown dog ran quickly across the field.
questions.explanation: The improved sentence adds clear details about the dog, action, and place.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve simple sentences by adding meaningful details.

questions.prompt: Read: Although the sun was hot, the players continued training. What does although show?
questions.explanation: Although introduces an idea that contrasts with what follows.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret connectors that show contrast in short texts.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would fit best in a paragraph about caring for a school garden?
options: Learners should water the seedlings every morning.
A drum can make a loud sound.
questions.correctAnswer: Learners should water the seedlings every morning.
questions.explanation: This sentence supports the topic of caring for a school garden.
questions.learningOutcome: Select supporting sentences that match a paragraph topic.

questions.prompt: Which option changes this direct speech correctly? Teacher said, "Open your books."
options: Teacher told us to open our books.
Teacher told us open your books?
Teacher open your books said us.
questions.correctAnswer: Teacher told us to open our books.
questions.explanation: The reported sentence keeps the meaning and changes your to our.
questions.learningOutcome: Change simple direct commands into reported speech.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the best word choice for a story opening?
options: Early one misty morning, we set off for the river.
questions.correctAnswer: Early one misty morning, we set off for the river.
questions.explanation: This opening gives time, mood, and action, making the story more interesting.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose vivid opening sentences for simple stories.

questions.prompt: Read: The new pupil felt nervous, so Rehema smiled and invited her to play. What can you infer about Rehema?
questions.explanation: Rehema helped the nervous pupil feel welcome, which shows kindness.
questions.learningOutcome: Infer character traits from actions in short texts.

questions.prompt: Which revision removes the repeated word? The small small boy carried water.
options: The boy small small carried water.
The small boy carried carried water.
Small small the boy carried water.
questions.explanation: Removing the repeated word makes the sentence clear.
questions.learningOutcome: Revise sentences to remove unnecessary repetition.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the clearest cause and effect?
options: The bell rang, so the learners went to class.
The bell rang and red quickly.
The bell was round and metal.
questions.correctAnswer: The bell rang, so the learners went to class.
questions.explanation: The sentence clearly shows that the bell ringing caused the learners to go to class.
questions.learningOutcome: Write or choose sentences that show cause and effect clearly.

questions.prompt: Which title best fits this sentence? We planted trees, collected litter, and swept the school compound.
questions.explanation: The actions all relate to caring for the school environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose a suitable title from the main idea of a short text.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best combines description and action?
options: The brave girl crossed the narrow bridge carefully.
The girl was bridge and crossed.
questions.correctAnswer: The brave girl crossed the narrow bridge carefully.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses describing words and an adverb to give a clear action.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose fluent sentences that combine description and action.
